title: engine: GraphBuilder.connect accepts mismatched counts, out-of-range slices, unknown type names and duplicate edges
description: engine/graph.py:529-546 with ports.py:142-166, 220-233. All of these compiled (reproduced): a fixed-512 output into a fixed-3 input (counts never compared; min_count/max_count/validate_range are never called by the graph); slices [600:900] on those ports; an input declared InputPortSpec('colour') (an unknown type name resolves to () and accepts_payload_type then returns True); a 1-column MatrixPayload into a 4-component HSBK port (every color class's is_compatible_with accepts any MatrixPayload); the same edge added twice; two unsliced edges into one port, where the second silently overwrites the first. Column mismatches are truncated silently at graph.py:208 and :268. reset_registries() (registry.py:205) leaves the payload registry empty, which turns every string-typed check into accept. Overlaps with the decisions in rasl-qvv.2 and rasl-qvv.3 for color typing.
design: Owner, 2026-11-14 (answering which accepted-today connections must be hard errors at load): 'Slice out of range, Unknown type name'. Fixed-count mismatch and overlapping destinations were offered and not chosen: their rule is still open, do not make them errors without asking.
acceptance_criteria: connect/build fail with a located error for: unresolved type name, count mismatch between fixed ports, slice outside a fixed port, duplicate edge, overlapping destination ranges, component-count mismatch. Each has a test.
notes:
Owner, 2026-11-14: scheduler and connect issues are 'core framework concerns that must be rock solid'; raised to P0.
Done 2026-11-15: GraphBuilder.connect refuses a slice past the end of a sized port and a port naming an unregistered payload type; the loader places every connect error on the connecting node (code rasl/connect). Tests: TestConnectValidation (tests/test_graph.py), TestConnectErrorsArePlaced (tests/test_channel_slicing.py). Still open, undecided: fixed-count mismatch, overlapping destinations and duplicate edges, component-count compatibility for color ports, silent column truncation, reset_registries() emptying the payload registry.
Owner 2026-11-16: duplicate edges, overlapping destinations and fixed-count mismatch are load errors too ('I agree with the first 3'). Done 2026-11-16 in GraphBuilder.connect: _check_count (fixed source rows x repeat vs fixed target rows or slice lengths; repeat_until edges not compared; a variable side not compared; replaces the old both-slices length check, which ignored repeat), _check_no_overlap (identical edge = duplicate; target rows [start, end) where end is the slice end, else start+repeat_until, else start + fixed source rows x repeat, else the end of the port, so two unsliced edges into one port overlap). Tests: TestConnectCountsAndOverlaps (tests/graph/test_builder.py), test_two_connections_into_one_port_... (tests/config/test_connect.py). Every example config still loads. Still open: color component count (owner: 'needs more clarification', see rasl-qvv.2), silent column truncation, reset_registries() emptying the payload registry.
Component count: done 2026-11-16 by rasl-qvv.3's matrix->color rule. Left open here: silent column truncation for non-color ports, reset_registries() emptying the payload registry.
close_reason: Done: slice out of range, unknown type name (2026-11-15), duplicate edges, overlapping destinations, fixed-count mismatch (a8da3f1), color component count (b7e6616, rasl-qvv.3). Remaining two items moved to rasl-pd0.44.

title: engine: repeat on a sliced connection resolves to the wrong edges
description: engine/graph.py:677-714. Reproduced: 'connect a[4:] i[0:] repeat=2' on a fixed-10 output yields source slices [0:10] twice with targets at 0 and 10: the start offset 4 is discarded (line 686 replaces the slice) and the length used is 10, not 6. On a variable-count output with repeat=3 it yields three identical edges [4:] -> [0:], so the copies overwrite one another and nothing repeats.
acceptance_criteria: A sliced repeat keeps the written slice and uses its length; when the length cannot be known at compile time the connection is rejected with a clear error (or resolved at run time, owner to choose). Tests cover fixed and variable outputs.
notes:
Owner, 2026-11-14: scheduler and connect issues are 'core framework concerns that must be rock solid'; raised to P0.
2026-11-21: the config layer had the same bug: resolve_connections (config/connect.py) expanded 'connect w[2~] { repeat 3; }' on a fixed-count source as w[0~4] three times. Fixed with rasl-00l (keeps the slice start, length = count - start); test tests/graph/test_counts.py test_a_repeat_of_an_open_slice_keeps_its_start.
close_reason: Fixed by the routing rewrite (RepeatSliceOp keeps the slice's start and length; a repeat on a source of unknown length is a located error since 37f4fb5). Regression tests in tests/graph/test_routing.py (TestRepeatSliceOp, test_a_sliced_repeat_through_the_builder_keeps_the_slice).

title: runtime: a graph with no rate-driving sink never runs any node
description: With no @pull_rate node, UnifiedScheduler runs _run_push_only (runtime/unified.py:664-674), which only drains the legacy inject() queue into the caches. No pull() is ever called, so source -> transform -> non-rate sink does nothing, silently. handle() (the legacy push interface still declared by BaseNode and implemented by SacnSink, SineSource) is never called by this scheduler at all. Loading such a graph gives no warning.
design: Owner, 2026-11-14: a graph that nothing drives is "probably just a warning, because we still want the system to load in case the user wants to inspect the graph via the UI". Load succeeds; warn naming what will never run. No push-driven execution.
acceptance_criteria: Either such a graph is rejected at load with a clear error naming the sinks, or push-driven execution is implemented (owner decision); nodes that are never reachable from a rate driver are reported.
notes:
SacnSink is the concrete case: see the sacn sink bead in this epic.
Owner, 2026-11-14: scheduler and connect issues are 'core framework concerns that must be rock solid'; raised to P0.
close_reason: The graph loads; UnifiedScheduler logs nodes_never_pulled (at start and after each plan update) and 'rasl --validate' prints the same list (find_undriven). With no rate driver the scheduler waits for a plan update. Tests: TestWhatIsDriven. SacnSink itself is rasl-pd0.17.

title: runtime: TickContext.dt is always 0 for rate-driving sinks
description: _pull_sink sets runtime.last_invoke_time = now (runtime/unified.py:939-940) and then _pull_node computes dt = tick.wall_time - runtime.last_invoke_time for the same node (unified.py:1013), which is 0. Reproduced: a 7 Hz sink saw dt 0.0 on every pull. Upstream nodes get a correct dt. Also TickContext.t is the dispatch time, not the slot's target time, so t carries scheduling jitter and two sinks in one slot see different t.
acceptance_criteria: A sink's dt equals the time since its previous pull; decide whether t should be the slot target time; tests cover both.
notes: Owner, 2026-11-14: scheduler and connect issues are 'core framework concerns that must be rock solid'; raised to P0.
close_reason: dt is the tick time since that node last ran, for sinks too; t and wall_time are the tick's due time, not the wake-up time. Test: TestTicks.

title: runtime: an over-budget tick starves the event loop; no frame dropping, cannot be cancelled
description: When pulls take longer than the slot interval, _run_scheduled (runtime/unified.py:703-806) finds every next target_time already past, so it never reaches an await that yields. Late slots are replayed one by one forever (lag grows without bound) and nothing else on the loop runs: Ctrl-C/SIGTERM handling, the web server, config watch, node background tasks. Reproduced: a 50 Hz sink whose pull blocks 30 ms; anyio.move_on_after(3) never fired and the process had to be killed. Any CPU-heavy numpy graph over budget hits this.
design: Owner, 2026-11-14: when a sink's due time is more than one period in the past, jump to its next future due time ("Yes, jump"); do not replay missed ticks. dt carries the real elapsed time. The scheduler's job is thin: "computing tick times and sharing the tick dt with each transformer".
acceptance_criteria: The loop yields at least once per tick; when behind by more than one interval it skips to the next due slot (policy to confirm with owner: drop vs. catch up) and logs/counts dropped ticks; test with an over-budget sink that cancellation works.
notes: Owner, 2026-11-14: scheduler and connect issues are 'core framework concerns that must be rock solid'; raised to P0.
close_reason: DueTimes.advance jumps a driver more than one period late to its next due time; the loop yields on every tick; dropped due times are counted (TimingStats.dropped_ticks, in timing_report) and logged at most once a second (ticks_dropped). Test: TestOverload.

title: runtime: rates that do not divide a one-second cycle are scheduled wrong
description: _build_schedule (runtime/unified.py:364-399) lays ticks out in a fixed 1.0 s cycle that restarts every second. Reproduced: 0.5 Hz sink is pulled at 1 Hz; 2.5 Hz sink gets intervals 400, 400, 200 ms; 7 Hz gets 142-144 ms plus a short last interval. ConsoleSink only allows fps >= 1, but any fractional fps (29.97, 2.5) is affected, as is any sink below 1 Hz.
design: Owner, 2026-11-14: chose per-driver due times ("the second fix does make more sense"): each rate driver's next due time is t0 + n/hz from one shared t0; drivers due at the same instant share one tick; no one-second table. Shared phase origin is kept so sinks that share upstream nodes stay aligned. Nodes must not assume a fixed dt: "driving nodes 'as little as possible' (based on sink requests) seems like the most efficient mechanism". A shared upstream node runs at the union of its sinks' timelines and gets the real dt.
acceptance_criteria: Each sink is pulled at its declared interval for any positive rate (per-sink next-due times, or a cycle of the rates' true common period); test with 0.5, 2.5 and 7 Hz.
notes: Owner, 2026-11-14: scheduler and connect issues are 'core framework concerns that must be rock solid'; raised to P0.
close_reason: Per-driver due times t0 + n/hz (runtime/unified.py DueTimes); the one-second slot table is removed. Tests: TestDueTimes, TestTicks.

title: runtime: a push source's write makes the scheduler busy-spin at 100% CPU
description: OutputPort.write on a push source calls UnifiedScheduler._on_push_write (runtime/unified.py:489), which sets _has_pending_push. Only the legacy inject() queue path ever clears the flag (unified.py:741-743). Once set, the sleep loop at unified.py:716-723 does sleep(0) and breaks on every pass until the next slot is under 1 ms away, so the process spins. Reproduced: SineSource(fps 2) -> ConsoleSink(fps 2) used 3.97 s CPU in 4 s wall; the same sink alone used 0.06 s. 'rasl virtual.conf' sits at 100% CPU. The wake has no purpose either: a push never triggers a pull, it is only read at the next scheduled tick.
design: Owner, 2026-11-14: "Sources don't drive the rates, sinks do." A push write only stores the latest frame; it never wakes the scheduler or causes a tick. Sinks read it at their next tick.
acceptance_criteria: A graph with a push source idles near 0% CPU between ticks; a regression test measures or asserts the sleep path. Decide (owner) whether a push should trigger an early tick or only be picked up at the next slot.
notes: Owner, 2026-11-14: scheduler and connect issues are 'core framework concerns that must be rock solid'; raised to P0.
close_reason: A push write only stores the port's latest frame (UnifiedScheduler._on_push_write, inject); the wake flag and push queue are gone. Test: TestPush in tests/test_unified_scheduler.py. virtual.conf now idles (1 s CPU in 7 s, startup included).

title: sacn: SacnUniverse source node replaces SacnSource
description: One universe per node. Outputs: raw channel vector (default port), count (RollingCounter, advances per packet received, identical data included), terminated (bool, true after a stream-terminated packet until data resumes). Joins the universe's multicast group always (owner, 2026-11-20); unicast still received. Shares the receiver per (bind_address, bind_port) via the resource registry. Updates family_room.conf and hyperhdr.conf. Supersedes rasl-pd0.19 (multicast, raw output; loss policy is now graph wiring) and rasl-pd0.20 (shared receiver).
notes:
Owner, 2026-11-20: 'Ideally SacnUniverse would offer both input ports and output ports and could be used as both a source and a sink.' One node type for both directions; the sink rework (rasl-2lg.5) becomes the send side of this node.
2026-11-21: receive side delivered (4089815) and SacnSource deleted; send side waits on the owner's pacing choice.
close_reason: Delivered on PR #19: SacnUniverse receives and sends one universe; SacnSource and SacnSink removed.

title: nodes: Reshape regroups a matrix's values into rows of N components
description: Owner agreed 2026-11-20: SacnUniverse emits a raw channel vector; Reshape { components 3; } groups it for Color. Remainder rule to confirm.
design: Owner, 2026-11-20: a value count not divisible by components is an error: at load when the count is fixed, else the node fails at pull. Row-major flatten then regroup.
close_reason: Delivered on PR #19 (claude/focused-darwin-jhjq77), 2026-11-21.

title: runtime: resource registry on NodeContext for shared transports
description: Nodes that share a socket or connection (sACN receiver/sender per bind port; later Govee, LIFX, DDP) acquire it from a registry the runtime passes on NodeContext, reference-counted, closed when the last holder releases and at runtime shutdown. Owner chose this over a module-level cache, 2026-11-20. Interface proposed in the PR before code.
design: Owner, 2026-11-20: a resource left with no holders during a live reload is closed only after the swap completes (no socket close/reopen, no multicast gap). Interface: Resources.acquire(key: ResourceKey[T], open, close) -> Lease[T]; Lease.release() idempotent; concurrent acquires share one open; open failure propagates and is not cached; runtime stop closes leftovers and logs them as leaks. Protocol in graph, implementation in runtime.
close_reason: Delivered on PR #19 (claude/focused-darwin-jhjq77), 2026-11-21.

title: signal: RollingCounter payload type
description: Owner, 2026-11-20: a wrapping counter must be an explicit type, not a float other nodes must know wraps. Carries value and modulus; defines advanced_since(previous); no implicit coercion to or from MatrixPayload. A flipping bit was rejected: two writes between reads alias to 'no change'.
close_reason: Delivered on PR #19 (claude/focused-darwin-jhjq77), 2026-11-21.

title: sacn: one node per universe on shared, runtime-owned transports
description: Owner decisions, 2026-11-20. Each node has one responsibility; complex behaviour is wiring, repeated wiring is a snippet. sACN packets are per universe, so the nodes are per universe and share one transport per (bind address, port) through a runtime resource registry. Cross-universe merge and split are graph wiring (non-overlapping connect ranges), not node config; this reverses the 2026-11-15 merged 'channels' default. Stream-loss policy (blank, hold, fallback) is not the source's job: the source exposes facts (a RollingCounter per packet, a terminated flag) and downstream nodes decide. Sources emit raw channel vectors; RGB grouping is downstream (Reshape).
notes:
Owner answers to the design's §11, 2026-11-20 (design: architecture workflow wf_223e3f88-44f, synthesized from minimal-framework + protocol-first):
Q4 agreed: receive arbitration, highest priority wins; at equal priority the first-seen source holds until it terminates or is silent 2.5 s (lazy, no timer).
Q5 agreed: count advances on accepted 0x00 data packets from the winning source only.
Q9 agreed: destination unset = multicast 239.255.hi.lo; universe 0 requires a destination.
Q10 ok: own E1.31 codec in devices/sacn/protocol.py; delete shims.py; no multicast join for universe 0.
Q14 agreed: multicast join failure warns and continues unicast-only; sendto OSError raises into pull.
Q16 agreed: dmx is both the input and an output name if PortGroup and the editor resolve it (proved by a test).
Q20: two nodes sending one universe is a construction (load-time) WARNING, not an error: needs a cross-node check at build, not SacnClaimError at start.
Owner, 2026-11-20: take the design's §11 recommendations for Q1-3, Q6-8, Q11-13, Q15, Q17-19, Q21 ('Take all but pacing'). Pacing (§5, Q2's driver choice) stays OPEN: the owner will choose; the send side waits for it.
2026-11-21: all eight children delivered or filed; PR #19 carries rasl-2lg.1-.5. Open: .6 (Changed/Since), .7 (snippet), .8 (Color raw vector), rasl-2lg.9, rasl-2lg.10, rasl-2lg.11.
Owner, 2026-11-21 (review): (1) pushed outputs approved; (2) Color width mismatch -> load error pointing to Reshape; (3) new SacnUniverse warnings ok; (4) 'Prioritize consistency and short direct names': destination->target, min_interval_ms->fps (frequency, 1-1000 Hz, default 40hz), sync_universe->sync, multicast_ttl->ttl, bind_address->bind. Supersedes Q9 and Q11.
Audit 2026-11-22: rasl-2lg.8 and .11 are closed. Open: .6, .7, .9, .10, .12 (all P2-P4).

title: web: canvas nodes can stay hidden after a reload; browser tests race the layout
description: CI on alpha (run 44010058084) failed 'a connection the graph refuses...' once. Two causes found under CPU load: (1) the test's settle check could pass before the ELK layout arrived; (2) React Flow kept rebuilt nodes visibility:hidden because their measured size was not passed back (the app rebuilds node objects every render and did not handle onNodesChange).
close_reason: Fixed: measured sizes kept via onNodesChange; canvas data-layout=ready after layout+fit; tests wait for it. 24/24 under 4 busy CPU loops.

title: nodes: ColorCorrection is a silent no-op or crashes on every color payload
description: nodes/color/correction_node.py:161-174 uses len(data) % 3 and len(data)//3 on (N,3) data, where len is the pixel count. Reproduced: 2 pixels with gamma 2.2 pass through unchanged; 3 pixels raise 'cannot reshape array of size 9 into shape (1,3)' on every tick. The node has no tests. It is also the only importer of nodes/color/convert.py, a stale 1049-line copy of engine/_color_convert.py that disagrees with it ('rgb' means sRGB there, linear in the engine) and lacks rgbw, hsbk and rec709.
acceptance_criteria: ColorCorrection works on payload rows, converts through the payload to_model API, nodes/color/convert.py is deleted, and tests cover gamma, each model and odd pixel counts.
close_reason: ColorCorrection works on pixel rows through the payload API; nodes/color/convert.py deleted; tests added.

title: nodes: Waveform crashes when phase or speed is connected; per-channel speed jumps every base cycle
description: nodes/effects/waveform.py:162-190. Reproduced: SeededRandom -> Waveform.phase (the use the class docstring shows) raises 'could not broadcast input array from shape (4,4) into shape (4,)' every tick, because (N,1) payloads are added to an (N,) phase. Separately the base phase is wrapped to [0,1) before it is multiplied by speed (:156, :173): sawtooth 1 Hz with speed 1.5 gives 0.485 at t=0.99 and 0.000 at t=1.00 (expected 0.500). TwinkleEffect multiplies before wrapping.
acceptance_criteria: Modulation inputs are flattened; phase is (frequency * t * speed + offset) % 1; tests run pull() with real payloads and check continuity across a cycle boundary.
close_reason: Modulation inputs are flattened to one value per channel, and speed scales the cycle count before the phase is wrapped (in float64). Tests: tests/nodes/test_waveform_node.py.

title: nodes: MathNode never produces output
description: nodes/effects/math.py:87-138 implements only the legacy handle() and ctx.emit; it has no pull(), and UnifiedScheduler calls only pull(). Reproduced: Waveform -> Math (multiply, constant_b 0.5) -> sink reads None on every tick, with no error. The tests call _apply_operation directly, so they pass. Its len()/np.resize logic also assumes 1-D payloads, while MatrixPayload is 2-D.
acceptance_criteria: MathNode implements pull() on inputs a/b with shape rules for (N,C) payloads confirmed with the owner; a test runs it under UnifiedScheduler.
close_reason: MathNode implements pull(); tests in tests/test_math_and_correction_nodes.py. Shape rule chosen while the owner was away (flagged in the PR): equal shapes as they are, numpy-broadcastable shapes broadcast, else the smaller input repeats to fill the larger.

title: govee: client speaks TCP with newline JSON; the Govee LAN API is UDP
description: packages/govee/client.py:185 uses socket.create_connection (TCP) to port 4003 and frames messages with newlines. The public Govee LAN API is UDP: multicast scan to 239.255.255.250:4001, device listens on UDP 4003, replies to UDP 4002. The client also sends a 'segments' array and a 'w' key in colorwc (client.py:96, node.py:284-303) that the API does not define. Proven by reading against the public spec; not tested on a device. If the owner's devices do answer on TCP, close this with a note.
acceptance_criteria: Owner confirms against a real device. Client follows the LAN API over UDP; per-segment output has a decided mechanism or is removed; encoder tests.

title: govee: blocking socket I/O on the event loop stalls every sink
description: packages/govee/node.py:97 calls the synchronous discover() in start(); reproduced with a silent 127.0.0.1 peer: start() took 2.00 s with a 2.01 s event-loop stall. In pull(), send_color_command does sendall with a 2 s timeout and, after any failure, a blocking create_connection (2 s) on every backoff expiry (client.py:140, 168, 185), so an unreachable device freezes all output repeatedly. While backing off, every tick raises ConnectionError (client.py:137) and logs govee_send_failed at error level at full fps (node.py:215-225).
acceptance_criteria: No blocking call on the loop (asyncio transport or worker thread); failure logging is rate-limited; a test with an unreachable device shows other sinks keep their timing.

title: sacn: two SacnSource nodes on one port, one silently receives nothing; receiver thread writes scheduler state
description: Each SacnSource creates its own sACNreceiver socket (packages/sacn/source.py:133-140) with SO_REUSEADDR on the same UDP port; unicast datagrams reach only one. Reproduced: adding a second node for universe 2 made the first receive None, with no error. Separately (suspected, not reproduced): the sacn library calls _listener on its own thread (:145-185), which calls OutputPort.write -> UnifiedScheduler._on_push_write, mutating _previous_outputs and _has_pending_push while the event loop reads them; self._loop is captured but unused. The per-universe port and the merged channels port update non-atomically.
acceptance_criteria: One shared receiver per bind port across nodes (or duplicate ports rejected at load); frames are handed to the loop with call_soon_threadsafe or a locked latest-frame slot; test with two sources.
notes:
2026-11-20: the receiver-thread half is fixed: SacnSource._make_listener hands each frame to the loop with call_soon_threadsafe and _publish writes the ports (src/rasl/devices/sacn/source.py; test tests/devices/test_sacn_source.py). Still open: two SacnSource nodes on one bind port. Paths in this bead's description predate the reorg (packages/sacn -> src/rasl/devices/sacn).
2026-11-20: superseded by the per-universe redesign, epic rasl-2lg (source: rasl-2lg.4; sink: rasl-2lg.5).
close_reason: Fixed by the shared SacnReceiver per (bind_address, port) (rasl-2lg.4); frames handed to the loop with call_soon_threadsafe.

title: sacn: sink is one universe, 512 channels, unicast only
description: packages/sacn/sink.py:57, 90-94, 109-111: one target_universe; data past 512 channels is silently truncated, so more than 170 RGB pixels cannot be sent; target_host is required and multicast is never enabled; no per-universe priority or sync. docs/user-guide.md:162-213 describes multi-universe fan-out and start_channel that do not exist.
acceptance_criteria: Design proposed and confirmed with owner (universe splitting rule, start channel, multicast flag, priority); implemented with loopback tests.
notes:
Owner, 2026-11-20: 'Sacn is more pressing than govee'; raised to P1.
2026-11-20: superseded by the per-universe redesign, epic rasl-2lg (source: rasl-2lg.4; sink: rasl-2lg.5).
close_reason: Superseded by SacnUniverse (rasl-2lg): one universe per node, multicast or unicast, priority per node, sync; splitting a long strip is connect ranges.

title: sacn: SacnSource never joins multicast, hard-codes RGB, and holds the last frame forever when the stream stops
description: packages/sacn/source.py:133-140 only calls register_listener; join_multicast is called nowhere in the package (grep), so standard multicast E1.31 senders are not received though the docstring (:45) says multicast. Every universe is reshaped to 170 RGB triplets (:152-160): 2 channels dropped, non-RGB layouts unreadable. No 'availability' listener, so a stopped or terminated stream leaves the last frame in place with no timeout or signal. On Linux the sacn library ignores bind_address.
acceptance_criteria: Multicast join per configured universe (flag to confirm); a raw-channel output; stream loss handled by a decided policy (hold, blank, or signal) with a timeout option; tests.
notes:
2026-11-20: superseded by the per-universe redesign, epic rasl-2lg (source: rasl-2lg.4; sink: rasl-2lg.5).
Stream-loss policy is no longer the source's: it exposes count and terminated ports; blank/hold is graph wiring (rasl-2lg.6, rasl-2lg.7).
close_reason: Superseded by SacnUniverse (rasl-2lg.4): joins multicast per universe, raw channel output, stream loss exposed as count/terminated for wiring downstream.

title: sacn: SacnSink never transmits DMX under UnifiedScheduler
description: packages/sacn/sink.py implements only the legacy handle() (:96) and has no @pull_rate pull(), so the scheduler never calls it (see the no-rate-driver bead). Reproduced: Waveform -> SacnSink to 127.0.0.1 for 2.5 s logged running_push_only_mode and sent 6 E1.31 packets, all zeros (the sacn library's keepalive). handle() is also wrong if called: the input port is hard-coded 'dmx' (:69) while input_port defaults to 'input' and is only a filter (:97), so frames are discarded; and MatrixPayload is 2-D, so line 108 raises 'could not broadcast input array from shape (10,3) into shape (10,)'.
acceptance_criteria: SacnSink is a @pull_rate sink like DdpSink, flattens its input, builds its port from input_port, and a loopback test receives the expected DMX bytes.
notes: rasl-pd0.5 is closed as a warning only: SacnSink still needs to become a @pull_rate sink.
close_reason: SacnSink is a @pull_rate sink (rate from min_interval_ms), flattens rows in order, and its input port carries the configured input_port name. Tested with a stand-in sender, not a socket (rasl-pd0.25 covers loopback tests).

title: color: conversions clip every result to [0,1], destroying Oklab a/b
description: engine/_color_convert.py:138 and :144 clip all non-HSBK conversion results to [0,1]. Oklab a/b are signed (frames/color.py:405 says [-0.4, 0.4]). Reproduced: sRGB green -> Oklab gives a = 0 (true value is negative); the round trip returns green as (1, 0.8, 0) and blue as grey (0.336, 0.336, 0.336). The existing Oklab test only uses values that survive the clip.
acceptance_criteria: Clipping is per target model (never Oklab a/b; Oklch as its ranges require); sRGB primaries round-trip through Oklab and Oklch within tolerance in tests.

title: engine: nodes of one class share that class's port objects
description: get_inputs / get_outputs (engine/nodes/protocol.py) fall back to the class-level PortGroup, so every node of a class that does not make its own ports shares the same InputPort and OutputPort objects. Seen while reviewing live reload: an old and a new SineSource object had the same outputs.dmx. Consequences today: OutputPort._node_id is the last-bound node's, so two push sources of one class (two SacnSource nodes) write _previous_outputs under one id; InputPort._has_upstream is 'any node of the class is connected'; a frame set for one node is readable by its siblings between pulls. The scheduler's _bind_ports now states and keeps that behaviour; the fix is per-node port objects.
notes:
Audit 2026-11-14, reproduced: three WaveformNodes (sine, square, sawtooth) share outputs.out; after pulling all three, the first node's frame holds the sawtooth values and np.shares_memory is True. Any graph with three or more nodes of a class using acquire/commit (Waveform, SeededRandom, SineSource) is corrupted; two only work because the two buffers alternate. Inputs bleed too: a second transform's unconnected port returned the first's frame with connected == True. BoundPortGroup.from_specs (engine/ports.py:644) already binds per instance and is unused.
2026-11-15: owner: 'Nodes own the Ports'. Per-instance port objects is the decided direction; lands with reorg phase 3 (rasl-39p.4).
close_reason: Each node owns its port objects: BaseNode.__init__ clones the PortGroups its class declares (PortGroup.clone), and get_inputs/get_outputs do the same lazily for nodes that are not BaseNodes. NodeHost.bind_ports no longer has to reason about shared ports. BoundPortGroup (unused) is deleted. Tests: TestNodesOwnTheirPorts in tests/test_runtime.py.

title: config: live reload, config file changes applied to the running graph
description: Owner, 2026-11-14: 'I want config file changes automatically reflected in the runtime graph, and in the future UI changes should also update the files and graph.' (2) a reload that fails keeps the old graph, all or nothing: 'Yes'. (3) runtime: 'Python'. (4) watching: 'On' by default. My defaults, not yet confirmed: a change outside any node (the ui block) is logged and ignored until restart; a connect-only change reroutes without restarting the node; a node whose own line changes (type, positional values) is replaced; the files as written are the one source of truth, so a future UI edit goes through knobly's edit-and-save and arrives by the same watcher.
notes: 2026-11-14 review round (PR 4): reload() no longer changes the session; commit(update) does, once the scheduler applied it. The scheduler works out the new schedule before stopping anything and refuses the update whole if that fails. Stopping a node cancels its background tasks and unhooks its outputs. A port that lost its last connection is cleared. The watcher keeps pre-reload stamps (a save during a reload is seen) and watches the files the last attempt read. A change outside any node is recorded without a swap. Not fixed: a node whose update_config raises keeps its old settings while the session records the new ones (logged as node_update_failed).

title: config: formal EBNF grammar as the language spec, proven sound
description: Owner, 2026-10-21: "I think we need a formal EBNF that describes the language so that we can prove its sound". Today the language is defined only by the handwritten lexer/parser (js/packages/config/src/lexer.ts, parser.ts) and prose rules in a deleted plan (now in rasl-m8w design). Code and the 'confirmed' rules already disagree (rasl-m8w.1). A formal grammar becomes the single definition; the TS parser and the later Python port are checked against it.
design:
Lexical decisions (rasl-m8w.1, rasl-m8w.2) are made while writing the grammar. Slice forms per rasl-9ze.1: [n:m], [n:], [:m]; [:] rejected. Relevant to rasl-k2e: an ANTLR4 .g4 grammar is one way to get an executable, checkable grammar.

Sound = both (a) grammar unambiguous and (b) parser accepts exactly the grammar's language. Owner, 2026-10-21: "Both. An EBNF gives a language independent syntax. And then parsers can be written against it, and then finally language-specific idiomatic sugar APIs can be layered on top".
Layers: (1) EBNF = language-independent syntax; (2) parsers per language written against it (TS first, Python port), each checked by the conformance corpus; (3) idiomatic per-language sugar APIs on top (in TS: AST facade, DirectiveDelegator, declarative definitions rasl-xlo).

Current shape (2026-10-22, PR #2, design/grammar/RECORD.md): Rasl.g4 (ANTLR4) is the spec; ANTLR4 generates TS and Python parsers; soundness (a) by .g4->Bison %expect 0 + token-overlap check in CI; (b) by construction plus a shared conformance corpus; lossless CST (document/directive/block/list/slice/error); custom recovery per language. Recommended-as-shown: depth limit 100 with its own code; a bad statement is one error node; error-code tidy (E2007 slice, new code for '{' on own line, E2002/E2005 emitted or removed).
acceptance_criteria: A versioned EBNF (lexical + syntactic) is the language-independent spec; a machine check proves it unambiguous (every valid input has one parse); grammar-generated positive and mutated negative inputs prove the TS parser accepts exactly the grammar's language and round-trips byte-identically; a conformance corpus with expected tokens/CST/diagnostics ships with it for other-language parsers.
notes:
Design in progress (2026-10-22): draft PR https://github.com/mcurcio/rasl/pull/2 (js/packages/config/design/grammar/). v1 failed adversarial review: Lezer is not EBNF and cannot express longest-match lexing; v2 drafts one plain-EBNF grammar file with all checks run on it.

Gate answers 2026-10-22: Q1 = B (recorded in rasl-m8w.1). Q2 (values must be separated) OPEN: owner picked A tentatively but noted "I can't answer confidently. I need concrete examples to review with points and counterpoints". Q3 (drop ANTLR4) OPEN: owner, 2026-10-22: "I want a formal language spec, but I don't care if it's EBNF. I'm ok with some other/better spec variant" and "I'm still hopeful we can build on some existing parser generator or code generator so that we can simplify the cross-language support." This supersedes the EBNF-specific wording of R1: the requirement is a formal, tool-checked language spec; notation is open.

Round 2 answers 2026-10-22: Q2 = A (recorded in rasl-9ze); Q3 = ANTLR4 if the CST is not sacrificed, otherwise hand-written parsers (recorded in rasl-k2e). Next: verification check of ANTLR (CST, .g4->Bison ambiguity check, recovery vs rasl-bzv.1).

design: Reserved: rasl, node, connect, type, input, output, segment, defaults, metadata. Identifiers /[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*/, case-sensitive; node names unique; port names unique per direction per node. At most one source per destination element; overlap = error; non-overlapping ranges into one port allowed. Length: both explicit -> equal else error; one open -> truncate to shorter; both open with a finite port -> finite remaining length; both open both variable -> error. No slice: equal fixed -> all; one variable -> finite size; both variable -> error. Error format: `config.conf:12:8: Overlap error` / line / caret / `input[0] already receives from nodeB.output[5]`. Use count terminology.

title: color: strict color-space compatibility and typed ColorNode output
description: Implement the decided rule. ColorNode's output port is declared generic ColorPayload (color_node.py:104), so downstream checks see 'any color', not the configured space. Sinks needing RGB (sACN, DDP, Govee) should declare it.
design: Input accepts any ColorPayload subclass; output type = COLOR_SPACES[configured space], resolved at graph build (resolve_output_type). Identity conversion is a no-op fast path; a missing conversion is a clear error naming both types.

notes:
Source: plans/Native Color Support.md §ColorConvert Node
Implements rasl-qvv.2's rule (owner 2026-11-16): matrix -> color allowed when the column count equals the color's components; a mismatch is a config error. Needs: output ports declare their component count where it is known (Waveform, SacnSource universe, Compose, literal...), so the check runs at load. OPEN, ask the owner: for an output whose width is not known until it runs, check on the first frame (a runtime error, not a load error) or refuse the connection at load until the output declares its width.
Owner 2026-11-16: 'Refused when config loads if the sizes are known, or fail on first data if the ports are dynamic'. Done 2026-11-16 (matrix -> color part): FramePayload.coerces_from (ColorPayload: a concrete color type takes a plain matrix; not another color type, not generic ColorPayload); InputPortSpec.coercion_target (single accepted type only); OutputPortSpec.components declares a matrix output's width (Waveform 1, SacnSource universes/channels 3, literal its data, Compose its port count); GraphBuilder refuses a known width that differs (ConnectTypeError COMPONENTS); InputPortProgram.coerce checks every plain-matrix frame and hands it on as the color type, else ComponentsError, which fails the receiving node like a failing pull(). Coercible ports' sliced/repeated frames now keep the color type (part of rasl-qvv.1). Still open in this bead: typed ColorNode output, sinks declaring their color type.
Owner 2026-11-16 (later): 'the color coercion is not specific to color. all types have an inheritance chain and should be allowed to coerce a more general type to a more specific type implicitly'. Generalized: FramePayload.coerces_from(other) = other is a strict ancestor of cls; FramePayload/MatrixPayload.coerce retype (MatrixPayload checks a fixed components width); ColorPayload refuses into the generic ColorPayload (no model) and refuses a generic color of another model at runtime. InputPortSpec.coercion_target(type) picks the one accepted type that coerces from it (none or two: refused). InputPortProgram retypes per frame (cached per payload type) and raises CoercionError (replaces ComponentsError) for a frame it cannot take, which fails the node. Behaviour: a plain matrix now feeds a BoolPayload port as a mask (non-zero -> 1); tests/config/test_types.py updated.

title: color: may plain matrix and color ports connect without a converter?
description: Gap between the owner's rule and code. ColorPayload.is_compatible_with accepts any MatrixPayload (frames/color.py:115,212), and ColorPayload subclasses MatrixPayload, so every MatrixPayload port (e.g. SacnSink dmx, packages/sacn/sink.py:69) accepts any color space and every color port accepts raw matrices. The owner's example (sine -> HSL -> sACN RGB) needs a rule for raw<->color edges.

notes:
Source: plans/Native Color Support.md vs frames/color.py:115
Owner 2026-11-16: 'I like the ability to coerce a more general type (vector) into a more specific type (color) that inherits from it.' So a plain matrix may feed a color port without a converter. Open: what happens when the matrix's column count differs from the color's components (a 1-column matrix into 4-component HSBK).

And MatrixPayload.components is None: a matrix output does not declare its width at load, so the mismatch can only be found at load once outputs declare components. title: config: DirectiveDelegator typing and defaults

description: Arguments are flat tokens. The spec (plans/nextgen.md) defines bracket lists and postfix slices, but every consumer re-parses them: engine rasl.ts has coerceScalar and parseSliceTokens.
design:
Confirmed: slices are postfix with no whitespace (foo[0:3]); the lexer does not enforce adjacency today. Lists are bracketed and may span lines. Bracket expressions stay separate tokens in the CST; typed values are a view over token ranges, with spans. Allowed slice forms: per the D3 decision bead.

Allowed slice forms (decided 2026-10-21, rasl-9ze.1): [n:m], [n:], [:m]. [:] is rejected with a located diagnostic.

Owner answer, 2026-10-22 (grammar gate round 2, Q2): option A. Values must be separated by a space or comment; a slice must touch its word; punctuation ({ } ; , list brackets) may touch anything. So "a""b", name"x", [a][b], a[0:3]b and x a [0:3] are errors. Owner asked: "Why is 'connect foo[1];' an error?" (answered: [n] is not among the rasl-9ze.1 forms; adding it would be a fourth form, his call). Current choice, revisable.
acceptance_criteria: Each directive argument exposes a typed value (word, string, number, list, slice) per the language spec, with spans; engine coerceScalar/parseSliceTokens are deletable.

title: config: include-transparent directive view
description: Includes are resolved into a document graph, but there is no view that walks them in place. iterateDirectives (src/iterate.ts) flattens bodies into one stream, losing block nesting despite its doc comment. 'include' is hard-coded in parse.ts and iterate.ts. The engine loader (engine/src/config/rasl.ts) walks only graph.root, so nodes in included files are silently ignored.
design: Confirmed (nextgen, include.md): include is core. Resolution produces a document graph; an inlined view is a separate pass. Include paths are quoted string literals; the loader interprets them (globs included). Core sorts matches by resolvedPath, code-point ascending. Loader: (spec, { parentPath, depth }) => Promise<Array<{ source, resolvedPath }>>. parse is async-only and requires a loader. maxIncludeDepth default 16. Visited paths stop cycles. Loader failure gives a diagnostic and leaves the include unresolved. Included files stay separate nodes so each round-trips. DirectiveDelegator is the public hook for include processing. Tests use mock loaders covering success, missing file, depth limit, cycles, multiple glob matches, ordering, no matches.
acceptance_criteria: An AST view replaces each include with its targets' directives in place, preserving nesting; include handling is a registered directive, not a hard-coded name; the engine reads nodes from included files (test proves it).

title: graph: every port's element count is resolved when the plan is built
description: Owner, 2026-11-21: connection sizes are fixed once configuration is complete; assume every element count is knowable at config time. Today almost no output declares a count (Waveform, SeededRandom, SineSource know output_channels from config but declare 'variable'; Smooth, RangeMap, RandomMap, MatrixMultiply, ColorCorrection, Twinkle output as many elements as they receive, and same_as carries only the type), so the builder skips count checks on variable sides and a repeat on a source of unknown length is a load error.
design:
Decided (owner, 2026-11-21):
- L1: element counts are fixed when the plan is built; a port's length never depends on which sources wrote. Counts are assumed knowable at config time.
- P1: until a source's first write, the elements it would write are zero (as fixed-count ports already do). Applies to every port.

Proposed, to confirm before implementing:
1. Every source declares its output count from its config (Waveform/SeededRandom/SineSource output_channels, Literal from its value, SacnUniverse channels as today).
2. Every transform declares how each output count follows its inputs: the same as an input (extend same_as to carry count, or a separate rule), or from config (Reshape, Compose).
3. The builder propagates counts through the graph in topological order; a connection's size is then fixed and checked on both sides.
4. A port whose count cannot be resolved at load is a load error, naming the port and why.
5. Cycles: a back-edge must end at a port whose count is already resolved without it (or the cycle is a load error).
6. Routing then always knows a buffered input's length; the variable-length paths in InputPortProgram (sizing from the sources that wrote) go away.
Open: exact rule vocabulary for transforms; whether same_as gains count or a new field is added; error wording.
notes:
Owner, 2026-11-21: same_as carries both the payload type and the element count of the named input (option a); no separate count field.
Owner, 2026-11-21, semantics confirmed:
- count_of="<input>" (count only) beside same_as (type and count). ColorNode, ColorCorrection, Twinkle use count_of input; Crossfade count_of input0, input1 must match (load error).
- Sources take counts from config: Waveform/SeededRandom/SineSource output_channels, Literal its value's length; SacnUniverse/Cron already declared.
- Reshape, Math, Compose compute output counts from resolved input counts (a node hook).
- Math (option b): equal counts, or one side exactly 1 element (broadcast); output = the larger; else load error. A constant side takes the connected side's count.
- Compose (option a): all connected inputs share one count = the output count; fill ports take it; all-fill uses output_channels; mismatch is a load error.
- An input port's count = the furthest element its connections write (target slices, source count, repeats); a fixed-count spec must match.
- An unresolved count is a load error only where a connection needs it.
Owner, 2026-11-21: keep the looser back-edge rule (a back-edge whose source count is known sizes its port; only a loop of count-following nodes is refused).
Code review fixes (2026-11-22): hooks may return InputSize to pass on width (Math does), SeededRandom/SineSource declare one column; hook errors only count in a final pass over settled counts, and a port with an uncounted back-edge is unknown rather than partial; Reshape reports an unknown input width; start retries also run while nothing ticks (Runtime._idle), and the runtime has its own clock for tests; config repeats with no or an open target slice are one graph edge (sized by the resolver, so a source counted from its input can repeat); a source slice starting past the end names the slice as written.
close_reason: Element counts fixed at plan build (graph/counts.py), owner's semantics incl. count_of, Math (b), Compose (a), Crossfade match, looser back-edge rule. family_room.conf's crossfade (135000 vs 120, a config bug that already failed at run time) fixed to 150-pixel patterns.

Config sync_universe per sending node. Sync packet goes to the sync universe's multicast group, or unicast to each distinct destination (owner: 'Correct'). Rates in one sync group: equal or whole multiples are silent; other ratios warn at load (proposed; owner did not object). Receive-side sync is part of this PR (owner): data naming a sync universe is held until a sync packet from the same source; join the sync group on demand; lazy 2.5 s fallback to immediate delivery; count advances per accepted data packet, emitted with the release (owner: 'A, I think'). design:
Operations: addNode(type, id, settings) inserts 'node Type id { ... }'; removeNode(id) removes the node AND every connect line naming it (owner 2026-11-16: 'remove the connections with it'); connect(src node.port[slice], target, port, repeat?) adds a connect line in the TARGET's block (that is where the language writes routing); disconnect(edge) removes that line; renameNode(old,new) renames and rewrites references; setSetting is rasl-w18.

title: config: typed Duration and Frequency for node config fields
description: Owner, 2026-11-15: 'is there an easy mechanism for nodes to parse the "50ms" string into a typed Duration?' Not today: a node declares the field as str, adds a validator that calls parse_interval, and a getter that calls it again (SmoothNode does this twice, for smooth_period and slew_period; DdpSink, LIFX and Govee do the same for fps). parse_interval lives in engine/units.py (pint) and returns seconds as a float.
design: Proposed, not confirmed: annotated pydantic types beside the node config bases, e.g. smooth_period: Duration = Duration('50ms'), where the validated value is seconds as a float (or a small Duration class with .seconds) and the JSON schema says it is a duration. Same for Rate (Hz). To confirm before building: (1) float seconds or a Duration class; (2) parse_interval reads a bare number as Hz ('30' is 1/30 s): a Duration field should probably reject or read bare numbers as seconds, which changes what existing configs mean.
acceptance_criteria: A node declares a duration with one annotated field and no validator or getter; Smooth and the fps fields use it; errors name the field and the accepted units.
notes: Owner, 2026-11-15: 'i like typed objects, so Duration would be good and maybe also a Frequency type if its part of the core lexicon'. So: value objects (classes), not bare floats; Frequency included (fps is on every sink and source). Still to confirm: what a bare number and a cross-unit value mean for each type.
close_reason: engine/units.py now holds Duration (.seconds) and Frequency (.hz, .period): immutable value objects that pydantic reads from config text. Strict, as the owner confirmed ('yes, i love those error messages'): a Duration refuses a bare number and a frequency; a Frequency refuses a time; bare numbers are hertz. Smooth's smooth_period and slew_period, the fps of DdpSink, LifxSink, GoveeLight and ConsoleSink, and SourceNodeConfig.fps use them; their validators and getters are gone. parse_interval and parse_frequency are removed. Behaviour changes: 'smooth_period 30', 'smooth_period 30hz' and 'fps 20ms' are now load errors; a device sink's 'fps 0.5' now means 0.5 Hz (parse_interval read a bare number below 1 as seconds, so it meant 2 fps); device sinks accept a bare-number fps (their fields were str, which refused 'fps 30').

title: python: reorganise src/rasl into domain packages with one import direction
description: Restructure the Python runtime into domain packages (signal, color, graph, runtime, nodes, devices, config, app) with smaller files and a single allowed import direction, enforced by a test. The full proposal, layout, phases and open questions are in the design field. Nothing is to be moved until the owner answers the open questions.
design:
PROPOSAL, not decided (owner asked for a plan, 2026-11-15: "plan a restructuring / reorg of the code to be more domain driven, so we get smaller files/classes with clearer ownership"). Package names and the open questions below need the owner's answer before any move.

Why: four files hold a third of the code (engine/graph.py 1054, runtime/unified.py 1054, engine/_color_convert.py 1009, nodes/color/convert.py 1049, engine/ports.py 730), GraphBuilder is 644 lines and UnifiedScheduler 800, and the packages import each other in cycles: engine -> config (ResolvedSlice, ConnectionDescriptor, Directive), engine -> nodes (registry calls rasl.nodes._register_all_nodes), config -> nodes (config models), runtime -> config (PlanUpdate, ConfigSession).

Domains and the one direction they may import in (each may import only those above it):

1. signal: what flows. Frame, MatrixPayload, BoolPayload, the payload registry.
2. color: color models, conversions, color payloads. Imports signal.
3. graph: topology and the node contract. Ports, BaseNode + its config base models + NodeContext + TickContext + pull_rate, the node registry, Edge + Slice, GraphBuilder, ExecutionPlan, the compiled input routing. Imports signal.
4. runtime: executing a plan. Due times, the tick loop, pulling, node lifecycle, plan swap, diagnostics. Imports graph, signal.
5. nodes: the built-in node library (effects, color, debug). Imports graph, signal, color.
6. devices (today 'packages'): one package per protocol, each owning its wire client and its nodes: sacn, ddp, lifx, govee. Imports graph, signal, color.
7. config: the config language. knobly document, node directive -> Config, connect syntax, build a plan, reload/diff, file watch. Imports graph, runtime (to hand over a PlanUpdate); reaches nodes only through the registry.
8. app: cli, server (GraphQL), ui. The only place that wires everything together.

Proposed layout (src/rasl/):

  signal/      frame.py, payload.py (base + registry), matrix.py, boolean.py
  color/       models.py (names, normalize_model), payloads.py,
               convert/__init__.py (convert(), dispatch table), rgb.py (srgb, linear, rec709, rgbw),
               hsl.py, hsbk.py (kelvin), oklab.py (oklab, oklch), okhsx.py (okhsl, okhsv)
  graph/       ports/spec.py, ports/group.py, ports/port.py
               node/base.py, node/config.py (today nodes/models.py), node/context.py, node/tick.py, node/registry.py
               edge.py (Edge, Slice), builder.py (add, connect, validate), order.py (topological order and back-edges, once),
               plan.py (ExecutionPlan, describe), routing.py (CopySliceOp, RepeatSliceOp, InputPortProgram)
  runtime/     timing.py (DueTimes, find_rate_drivers, find_undriven), scheduler.py (the loop only),
               executor.py (pull a sink and its upstream, frame cache), lifecycle.py (start/stop/bind nodes),
               update.py (PlanUpdate and applying it), diagnostics.py (TimingStats, TickTrace, NodeMonitor)
  nodes/       effects/, color/, debug/, literal.py (one node per file, as now)
  devices/     sacn/, ddp/, lifx/, govee/ (client.py or protocol.py + node files)
  config/      document.py, units.py, node_directive.py (node syntax -> class + Config), connect/syntax.py (parser),
               connect/resolve.py (descriptors -> graph.connect), build.py (build_plan), reload.py (ConfigSession, diff), watch.py
  app/         cli.py, logging.py, server/, ui/

What moves to break the cycles:
- ResolvedSlice (config/connect_parser.py) becomes graph.edge.Slice: it is a graph value the parser produces.
- GraphBuilder.resolve_node_connections (reads config descriptors) moves to config/connect/resolve.py and calls GraphBuilder.connect.
- BaseNode.parse_connect_directives / _connection_descriptors: the loader keeps the descriptors, not the node (see open question 3).
- nodes/models.py (BaseNodeConfig and the Source/Transform/Sink bases) moves beside BaseNode.
- The registry stops importing rasl.nodes; built-ins load through the 'rasl.nodes' entry point pyproject already declares, like any plugin. nodes/__init__.py's 70-line lazy __getattr__ goes.
- PlanUpdate moves to runtime (it is the scheduler's input); config.reload produces it. watch_config moves to config.
- The second back-edge search in the scheduler goes; the plan carries the back-edges.

Phases, each one PR that only moves or deletes code, tests green, no behaviour change:
0. Guardrails: ruff config (F, I, B) and an import-layer contract test (import-linter) for the direction above, starting with today's violations listed as exceptions and removing them phase by phase.
1. Delete what is dead: legacy Runtime + handle()/emit (after rasl-8xm, rasl-pd0.26), nodes/color/convert.py (after rasl-pd0.27), lifx/manager.py (rasl-pd0.23 decision), BoundPortGroup unless rasl-e7j uses it.
2. Break the cycles (the list above).
3. Split graph.py and ports.py into graph/. Natural place to land rasl-e7j (per-instance ports) right after.
4. Split unified.py into runtime/.
5. signal/ and color/: split _color_convert.py by model family.
6. packages/ -> devices/; config/loader.py split; app/.
7. Public API: what 'import rasl' and each package's __init__ export; docs/node-development.md import paths.

Not shims: import paths change with no aliases (repo rule). External plugins and the tests update their imports in the same PR.

Open questions for the owner:
1. Names: signal / graph / devices / app, or keep engine / packages? (graph could also stay 'engine'.)
2. Is color its own top-level domain, or part of signal?
3. Who owns a node's connect directives: the loader (cleanest layering) or the node (rasl-9pn wants nodes to own their keywords via ConfigDispatch)? config/dispatch.py (291 lines) and config/channel_mapping.py (163) are used by nothing but their tests today.
4. Phase 1 deletions: confirm each.
5. Should the test tree mirror the packages (tests/graph/, tests/runtime/, ...)?
acceptance_criteria: No file over about 400 lines and no class over about 250 in src/rasl; the import-layer contract test passes with no exceptions; uv run pytest is green; no behaviour change across the series.

design:
# Proposal: tick-aligned double buffers on both port kinds, one naming scheme (rasl-pd0.12)

Revision 4, final. Two architect review rounds (both "approve with changes"); owner decisions
D1–D6 and Q1–Q3 applied (2026-11-21).

## 1. Problem

An input port fed by a slice, a repeat or several edges is built each pull into one scratch
array owned by the executor (`runtime/executor.py:139`), zero-filled and rewritten every pull
(`graph/routing.py:262-370`); a frame that outlives the pull changes under its holder. Outputs
double-buffer but swap on every `commit` (`graph/ports/port.py:150-168`), so a push source
committing from its background task (`nodes/debug/sine_source.py:76-86`) can recycle a buffer
a slow reader still holds within one tick. `ctx.inject` bypasses the port and writes `latest`
directly (`executor.py:118-122`). `ColorCorrection` forwards its input frame
(`nodes/color/correction_node.py:158`) into `latest`, where it outlives its source's buffer.
`Frame` claims immutability (`signal/frame.py:28`); only the dataclass is.

## 2. Constraints

- Throughput first: connections compiled at plan time; no extra copy or allocation per tick
  on pulled ports; data stays as views. (`populate` already allocates one `Frame` and one
  payload object per buffered input per pull, `routing.py:363-368`; unchanged here.)
- Layers: `graph` (ports, routing) → `signal`. The runtime drives ports and does not own their
  storage; `graph` reads no runtime config.
- Ticks run strictly in sequence (`runtime/runtime.py:231`), so the tick boundary is a point
  where no pull is running.

## 3. Design

### 3.1 Commit marks complete; the framework publishes (owner, 2026-11-21)

Buffers swap when the framework *publishes*, never when a node writes or commits.

- `acquire` returns the back buffer and clears *ready*. `commit(frame)` sets the pending frame,
  *ready* and *swap*. `write(frame)` sets the pending frame and *ready*, clears *swap* (the
  frame owns its data; no buffer is involved).
- `_publish()` (framework): if *ready*, make the pending frame the published one, swap
  front/back only if *swap*, clear *ready*, return the frame; else return None. Replaces
  `OutputPort._consume()` and `was_written`.
- **Pushed outputs** are those with `OutputPortSpec(pushed=True)`, plus every output of a node
  that has no `pull` (a pure push source such as `SineSource`). A node without incoming edges
  that does have `pull` (an unconnected `Waveform`, a literal) is pulled in the tick and is not
  pushed (today `lifecycle.py:91-97` hooks every such node).
- `executor.set_plan` precomputes, per node, its pulled outputs (published at the end of its
  pull, `executor.py:327`) and the pushed outputs of the whole plan (published in
  `begin_tick`), each with its `(node_id, port)` key, so neither loop builds tuples or calls
  `isinstance` per tick. Rebuilding the lists from the new plan's node objects also stops a
  replaced node from publishing under its successor's id.
- **Inputs**: `InputPortProgram.populate` calls `_commit` then `_publish` back to back (merged
  into `_commit` for inputs if the pd0.15 baseline shows the extra call matters).
- A port with nothing ready does not swap; nodes on slower rates are unaffected.
- A pull that raises clears its outputs' *ready* on the failure path (no normal-path cost),
  so the next pull that writes nothing does not publish the failed pull's frame (closes
  rasl-v1e; Q3: owner, fold in).
- `executor.forget()` stops calling `begin_tick()` (which now publishes); it calls a new
  `_clear_tick_cache()`, deletes `latest` for stopping nodes, and leaves kept nodes' buffers.

Producer rules (documented): do not await between `acquire` and `commit` (a producer mid-fill
at a tick boundary is skipped that tick; readers keep the previous frame); push producers run
on the event loop (no lock is added).

### 3.2 Push writes go through the port (Q1: owner, yes)

`ctx.inject(port, frame)` becomes `self.outputs.<port>.write(frame)` (or `acquire`/`commit`),
and is pending on the port until `begin_tick` publishes it. `store_pushed`, `on_push_write`,
`OutputPort._on_write` and its wiring (`lifecycle.py:97,168`) are deleted. `SacnUniverse`
(`devices/sacn/universe.py:333`) and the `NodeContext` docstrings move to port writes.

### 3.3 `FrameBuffers` (D1), and choosing the debug variant

New `graph/ports/buffers.py`: two flat float32 arrays that grow in capacity only; `acquire`
returns `flat[:rows*cols].reshape(rows, cols)` (always C-contiguous, never reallocated when
widths alternate). `FramePayload.ensure_buffer` remains the one allocator, called only to grow.

```python
class FrameBuffers:
    __slots__ = ("_front", "_back", "_pending", "_published", "_ready", "_swap", "_shape")
    def acquire(self, count: int, components: int) -> np.ndarray: ...
    def commit(self, frame: Frame) -> None: ...
    def write(self, frame: Frame) -> None: ...
    def publish(self) -> Frame | None: ...
    @property
    def previous(self) -> np.ndarray | None: ...
```

- Outputs: created at bind time; inputs: by `compile_input_programs` for non-passthrough ports
  only. Both receive a buffers factory passed explicitly through plan compile and bind, so the
  runtime chooses `FrameBuffers` or `DebugFrameBuffers` and `graph` reads no config.
- `OutputPort.acquire` caches its payload type and component count at bind time instead of
  calling `spec.resolve_payload_types()` per call (`spec.py:331`).
- No `release()`: ports of stopped nodes go with their nodes.

### 3.4 Incremental writes (D6 = c)

`OutputPort.previous` is a read-only view of the published front buffer: the frame readers
currently see. It is None before the first publish, after a publish that came from `write`, or
when its shape differs from the most recent `acquire` (stored by `acquire`).

```python
buf = out.acquire(n)
np.multiply(out.previous, 0.9, out=buf)   # decay last output, no extra copy
out.commit(Frame(..., payload=MatrixPayload(buf)))
```

For a push producer, `previous` is the last *published* frame, not its last commit: a source
committing four times a tick and decaying from `previous` decays once per tick. Incremental
push producers keep their own state. `acquire`'s contents are otherwise undefined.

### 3.5 Naming

Producer verbs on the side that produces a port's frame, reader verbs on the side that reads
it; a leading underscore is framework-only. Public names unchanged except Q1/Q2; no aliases.

| Layer | Produce (own data) | Get back buffer | Mark complete | Publish | Last published | No frame | Read |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `OutputPort` (author produces) | `write(frame)` | `acquire(count, *, components=None)` | `commit(frame)` | `_publish()` | `previous` | `_clear()` | — |
| `InputPort` (framework produces) | `_write(frame)` | `_acquire(count, *, components)` | `_commit(frame)` | `_publish()` | — | `_clear()` | `read(default=None)` |
| `FrameBuffers` | `write` | `acquire` | `commit` | `publish` | `previous` | — | — |

Renames: `InputPort._set_frame` → `_write` (never None; no frame is `_clear()`);
`OutputPort._consume` → `_publish`; `was_written` deleted. `commit` keeps its name but no
longer swaps.

### 3.6 Routing and executor (D3 = option 1)

- `InputPortProgram.populate(tick, resolve)` owns the input's publish: passthrough → `_write`;
  no source frame → `_clear`; buffered → acquire, zero, fill, `_commit` after every op and
  retype passed, then `_publish`.
- The `ensure_buffer` callback goes; `buffer_key` stays, renamed `endpoint`.
- `executor._port_buffers` and `_ensure_port_buffer` are deleted; `executor.py:294` no longer
  sets the frame.

### 3.7 Forwarding (D5 = b; Q2: named `detach`)

A node that writes a frame it did not build (an input frame, or another node's) calls
`frame.detach()` first: the data copied into a new array, topic, timestamp and metadata kept.
Cost falls only on forwarding nodes (`ColorCorrection`'s non-RGB path today).

### 3.8 Lifetime contract (docs/writing-nodes.md, `Frame` docstring)

> A published frame stays unchanged until its producer's first fill after its next publish.
> Pulled ports publish at most once per pull; pushed ports at most once per tick, at its start,
> so a frame read in a tick is unchanged for the rest of that tick. A frame built with `write`
> is never touched by the framework. An input fed by one whole connection carries its source's
> frame and lifetime. A node that keeps a frame past its next pull copies it; a node that
> writes a frame it did not build calls `frame.detach()`.

### 3.9 Debug check (D4)

`DebugFrameBuffers`, chosen through the factory (§3.3) when debug is on (runtime config flag;
`RASL_DEBUG_FRAMES=1` for tests):

- A fresh array on every `acquire`; the array leaving the two-slot window is filled with NaN.
  The executor binds a checking `_resolve_frame` in `set_plan` that asserts finite data on
  every read; sinks may assert too (values are in [0, 1]).
- `write` checks `payload.data.base` against the set of arrays debug buffers have allocated: a
  forward without `detach()` of any port-buffered frame (including passthrough inputs) raises.
  It cannot catch a frame built over a node-owned array the node reuses; documented.
- `commit` checks the frame views the current back buffer (catches a stale `acquire` view and a
  `commit` without `acquire`).

Zero cost off: `OutputPort.write` always delegates to its buffers' `write` (needed anyway for
§3.1), so debug is a different class and a different bound resolve, with no flag branch.

## 4. Throughput

- Pulled ports: same single fill per buffered input; no new allocation; output views
  contiguous; `OutputPort.acquire` loses a registry lookup per call; the collect loop loses an
  `isinstance` and a tuple per output; one extra call per buffered input (`_publish`), measured.
- Pushed ports: one ready check per pushed port per tick.
- Memory: one more array per buffered input port; passthrough inputs allocate nothing.
- Baseline first (pd0.15 step): fan-in of N sliced edges, a repeat, a long passthrough chain,
  a cycle, a 512-row output, a push source at 4x the tick rate; per-tick wall time and
  `enable_profiling` stats, re-run after.

## 5. Tests

- Input and output frames unchanged until the producer's first fill after the next publish.
- Push source committing several times while a sink's pull awaits: the sink's frame is
  unchanged for the tick; the next tick sees the latest push; mid-fill at the boundary leaves
  the previous frame published.
- An unconnected node with `pull` publishes in its tick, not at the next tick start;
  `SacnUniverse`'s pushed outputs publish only at tick start.
- No commit since last publish: no swap. `write` then publish: no swap; `previous` is None.
- A failed pull's pending frame is not published by the next pull that writes nothing.
- Plan swap: no publish inside `forget`; a kept node keeps its buffers.
- `previous`: decay node; None before first publish and after a shape change.
- `ColorCorrection` non-RGB forward uses `detach()`.
- Alternating input widths: no reallocation; outputs stay contiguous.
- Debug: poison fires on a stale read, on a forward without `detach()`, on a stale commit.

## 6. Behaviour changes (approved unless noted)

1. Input-built frames live one pull longer than today.
2. A push becomes visible at the next tick start, not mid-tick.
3. `commit` no longer swaps; `_publish` does. Renames per §3.5.
4. Nodes without incoming edges that have `pull` are no longer treated as push sources (their
   frames publish in-tick, as they are read today).
5. Buffers grow in capacity and are reshaped; no reallocation on width change.
6. A node kept across a plan swap keeps its buffers.
7. `ColorCorrection`'s non-RGB forward becomes a copy.
8. `ctx.inject` removed in favour of port writes (Q1).
9. A failed pull's written outputs are discarded (Q3, closes rasl-v1e).
10. Docs: "immutable" replaced by the lifetime contract.

## 7. Out of scope (filed)

- rasl-4q5: an output with one consumer writes straight into that input port's buffer.
- rasl-zcr: stale "color model" sentence in docs/writing-nodes.md.
- `BoolPayload.__init__` copies (`astype`) where other payloads wrap a view.

## 8. Owner decisions (2026-11-21)

D1 flat grow-only buffers; D2 renames; D3 populate owns the input publish; D4 NaN debug
check; D5 forwarding nodes copy (`frame.detach()`); D6 `OutputPort.previous`; tick-aligned
publish (owner's model); Q1 remove `ctx.inject`; Q2 `detach`; Q3 fold in rasl-v1e.
acceptance_criteria: A frame handed to a node is not mutated after the tick that produced it (double buffer as OutputPort does, or copy on escape); a test holds an input frame across ticks.

Buffered inputs pay ~0.4 us per pull for acquire+commit+publish (micro-benchmark); merging _commit/_publish would save ~0.1 us, so the symmetric API stays. Implementation deviations from rev 4: input buffers are given by NodeHost.bind_ports (runtime) from plan.input_programs rather than by compile_input_programs, so building a plan allocates nothing; the debug choice is the NodeHost's buffers class; the flag is the runtime block's debug_frames (no env var).
Baseline before the change (2026-11-21, alpha at dbd0980, 4-core x86_64 cloud container, scripts/bench_ticks.py defaults: 2000 ticks x 7 runs):

title: engine: runtime topology changes by background compile and safe swap
description: No support today: no plan generation or swap protocol (grep generation/swap in src/rasl finds nothing). Topology changes need a restart.
design: Monotonic plan generation id; ports and routing generation-tagged. On change: build ExecutionPlan, compile BoundExecutionPlan off the hot path (validate types/slices/count). Swap at tick boundary/idle: pause routing, reconcile lifecycles (keep, stop removed gracefully, start new), rebind ports, migrate buffers. Reuse a buffer only when payload type, dtype/components match and capacity suffices. Push writes never publish into the wrong generation. API: request_plan_update(plan_spec), poll_compiled_plan(), swap_if_ready_at_safe_point().
acceptance_criteria: A running UnifiedScheduler accepts a new plan, compiles it off the hot path, swaps at a tick boundary keeping unchanged nodes running, stopping removed and starting new ones, and drops old-generation push writes; integration test adds and removes a node without restart.
notes:

Not built from this bead's design: generation-tagged ports, compiling a BoundExecutionPlan, buffer migration (port buffers are dropped at a swap), dropping old-generation push writes.

title: engine: BoundExecutionPlan with port-bound edge ops
description: InputPortProgram (graph.py:293) resolves sources by node id each tick, allocates a new Frame and MatrixPayload per tick, zero-fills the whole view, no shared-subexpression reuse. design: BoundEdgeOp: source_port: OutputPort, target_port: InputPort, strategy, src_slice/tgt_slice (count), repeat / repeat_until; route(tick). Strategies at bind: identity, slice view (true view when possible), slice fill into target region, repeat fill (only needed region, no intermediate tiling; cache repeated segments per tick). Detect common subexpressions across edges. BoundExecutionPlan: generation, incoming_ops: dict[str, list[BoundEdgeOp]], schedule, node_runtimes. Edge type check at bind via FramePayload.is_compatible_with.
acceptance_criteria: Scheduler routes only through BoundEdgeOp.route(tick) from a BoundExecutionPlan; strategy chosen at bind; identical source+transform pairs compute once per tick; GraphBuilder.connect describes topology only; MatrixPayload.repeat removed; routing tests pass.

title: engine: complete the acquire/fill/commit output contract
description: acquire/commit exist (ports.py:563,594) but diverge: commit takes a Frame and re-checks payload type each call; acquire never rejects a count mismatch on fixed-count ports; only three nodes use it (waveform.py:188, sine_source.py:77, seeded_random.py:74), the rest allocate per tick via write(). No idle-time growth of the paired buffer.
design: buf = output.acquire(count) -> ndarray; node fills (ufunc out= encouraged); output.commit() -> None. Payload type comes from the port spec, never chosen at commit. acquire succeeds immediately; growth on the back buffer at once; publish swap only at a safe point. Fixed-count: buffers allocated upfront, acquire errors on mismatch. Dynamic: amortized growth, never shrink, may pre-size from graph info. Double buffering: front=published, back=writable. Track ports grown this tick; during scheduler sleep grow their paired buffers on the scheduler thread, then clear. OutputPort: acquire, commit, published(), capacity(); state front, back, logical_count, generation.
acceptance_criteria: Every built-in producer writes via acquire/fill/commit; fixed-count acquire(count != spec) raises; dynamic ports grow immediately and the paired buffer grows during scheduler idle; a test shows no steady-state per-tick allocation for waveform->sink.

title: engine: tick-cheap runtime and hot-swappable plans

notes:
Source: js/packages/config/plans/nextgen.md §3

Finding 2026-10-22 (grammar design, PR #2): 'resume next line' cannot hold for an unclosed '[' because lists may span lines; the error is only detectable at the next '}' or EOF. Acceptance wording needs changing (proposed on the round-2 gate page).

From the ANTLR check (2026-10-22): an unclosed '[' is reported at the next '}' or EOF only while the list contents stay valid (x [a,\n b\ny 1 fails at y). Codes to tidy: E2007 bad slice missing from tokens.ts; '{' on its own line needs a code; E2002/E2005 never emitted; touching values get generic E2001. Depth ~1000 crashes both runtimes: add a depth limit with its own code.

title: config: keep or drop ANTLR4 parser generator
description: plans/nextgen.md commits to ANTLR4 for cross-language ports. It adds a runtime dependency and complicates trivia preservation, while the handwritten parser already round-trips byte-identically. Recommendation: drop it; use the spec plus conformance corpus (packaging epic) for ports.
design:
nextgen.md lists as confirmed: 'Parser generator: adopt ANTLR4 and treat the .g4 grammar as the shared foundation for multi-language bindings.' Planned token model: raw text kept; whitespace/comments may sit on a hidden channel but stay accessible; newline is structural. Dropping ANTLR4 reverses a decision the plan marks confirmed; needs the owner's explicit call.

Outcome 2026-10-22: keep ANTLR4 (owner: "A is ideal if we don't sacrifice the CST. Otherwise, C."). Verification on 14,900 inputs: lossless CST in TS and Python, byte-identical CST and diagnostic JSON across languages, matches config.ebnf reference; ambiguity proven by mechanical .g4->Bison translation (%expect 0) plus a token-overlap check; custom recovery (~95 lines/lang) meets rasl-bzv.1. Runtime: official antlr4 4.13.2 (TS) + antlr4-python3-runtime 4.13.2, pinned. Record: js/packages/config/design/grammar/RECORD.md. plans/nextgen.md kept unedited as source material (owner: don't delete the plans).
acceptance_criteria: Owner decides; the outcome is recorded here and plans/nextgen.md updated or deleted.
notes:
Owner wants a formal EBNF to prove the language sound (see rasl-g7n); weigh whether ANTLR4 serves as the grammar checker. Owner, 2026-10-21: "I think we need a formal EBNF that describes the language so that we can prove its sound".

Owner, 2026-10-22 (grammar gate Q3, no option picked): "I want a formal language spec, but I don't care if it's EBNF. I'm ok with some other/better spec variant"; "I'm still hopeful we can build on some existing parser generator or code generator so that we can simplify the cross-language support." Re-opened: weigh generators that emit TS and Python parsers from one formal spec (ANTLR4, tree-sitter, REx, others) against the hand-written-parser shape.

2026-10-22 generator comparison (js/packages/config/design/grammar/v3-generators.md, v3-review.md): on 14,830 inputs ANTLR4 TS and Python matched the reference exactly incl. first-error offsets, pure runtimes, sync API; ANTLR builds ambiguous grammars silently, so (a) needs a CI check (.g4 -> Bison translation, not built). tree-sitter failed review (error offsets early in ~22% of broken inputs, TS/Py diverge on non-ASCII, recovery misses rasl-bzv.1 cases, wasm + native wheels). Round-2 gate recommends keeping ANTLR4 plus the CI check; awaiting owner.

Owner answer, 2026-10-22 (grammar gate round 2, Q3): option A (ANTLR4 generates the TS and Python parsers; Rasl.g4 is the spec; CI proves it unambiguous via a .g4->Bison translation), conditional: "A is ideal if we don't sacrifice the CST. Otherwise, C." (C = config.ebnf checked by REx/Bison, hand-written parsers). Pending a verification check that ANTLR keeps the full lossless CST (every token, round trip, our node kinds, separate slice tokens, error nodes) in TS and Python.
close_reason: Keep ANTLR4: owner chose it on condition the CST is kept; verification showed it is (see design field and design/grammar/RECORD.md).

notes: 2026-11-15, checked: Okhsl and Okhsv give the reference values for the sRGB primaries (s = 1; lightness 0.568, 0.845, 0.367) and round-trip sRGB to 1e-5. The primaries sit at the cusp, where the formula is right. Away from the cusp C_max is larger than the gamut's, and the output clip hides it, so s = 1 at other lightnesses is not the gamut boundary. Not fixed: it needs Ottosson's find_gamut_intersection.

design: Confirmed language rules (nextgen §Current decisions): newline ends a directive; semicolons optional, needed only for several directives on one line. No backslash line continuation. Comments: // and /* */ only (contradicted by code, see D1 bead). Dot is part of a word. Unquoted words: letters, digits, underscores, dots, no hyphens (contradicted by code, see D1 bead). Diagnostics: 0-based line/column, stable codes plus messages. Public API keeps the directive-level AST; no RASL node/connection AST. Core does no I/O. Spec deliverables: EBNF grammar plus lexical spec; versioned core profile; conformance corpus of inputs with expected tokens/CST/diagnostics as JSON. Milestone 0: generic README, RASL examples move to the consumer, neutral fixtures (e.g. server { listen 8080; }). Spec states the unit of offset and column.

design: Confirmed (nextgen, roundtrip): byte-identical serializeCst(parse(x).cst) === x is first-class. Trivia kept in CST. Canonical storage is the full token stream; directive nodes reference token ranges, never copy tokens. Tokens keep raw text and 0-based spans. Serialization is token concatenation; subtree = node's token range. Edits are token splices keeping spans stable; no trivia-attachment heuristics. Three tiers: power users edit tokens/CST byte-identically; most use the AST facade (edits may normalize formatting); minimal consumers use declarative registration (rasl-xlo). Tests: golden round-trip; mutation tests assert only intended token ranges change.
